answer: Each identity claims one region and proves it by latency triangulation: five landmarks measure round-trip times, and the result must fit that region within 20 ms, backed by a 12 POA deposit slashed on mismatch. A single machine cannot be in many places at once, so a fake that pretends to live in a distant haven fails its checks, while honest users pass from home. Every extra fake needs its own presence, or a rented relay whose delta grows with distance and cost, so 100 fakes cost 100 presences. A sparrow of doubt triggers a re-probe, and latency logs sit on-chain for any verifier to replay.
